merger_description:
Complete Air Supply Pty Ltd (**Complete Air Supply**) proposes to acquire 100% of the All Air Duct & Fittings Pty Ltd (**All Air**) business and assets (the **Acquisition**).

Complete Air Supply is a member of the Beijer Group, which operates throughout Australia in the refrigeration and Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (**HVAC**) industry. The Beijer Group supplies equipment and parts to the refrigeration and HVAC industry.

Complete Air Supply supplies HVAC units, and manufactures and supplies HVAC ductware and fittings, to installers for domestic residence installs or commercial air conditioning projects. HVAC ductware and fittings includes flexible ducting, sheet metal fittings, cushion boxes, grilles, diffusers, copper, zoning and accessories used by installers. Complete Air has four branches and operates primarily in Southeast Queensland and Northern New South Wales.

All Air manufactures and supplies HVAC ductware and fittings to installers for residential and commercial purposes. All Air has two branches and operates only in Southeast Queensland.

All Air supplies the same HVAC ductware and fittings products as those supplied by the Complete Air Supply but does not supply HVAC units.

determination_table_content.details:
Complete Air Supply Pty Ltd’s (Complete Air Supply) proposed
acquisition of 100% of the All Air Duct & Fittings Pty Ltd (All Air)
business and assets (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Complete Air Supply, supplies Heating, Ventilation, and
Air Conditioning (HVAC) units, and manufactures and supplies
HVAC ductware and fittings, to installers for domestic residence
installs or commercial air conditioning projects. Complete Air Supply
has four branches and operates primarily in Southeast Queensland
and Northern New South Wales.
Complete Air Supply is a member of the Beijer Group, which
operates throughout Australia in the refrigeration and HVAC
industry. The Beijer Group supplies equipment and parts to the
refrigeration and HVAC industry.
The target, All Air, manufactures and supplies HVAC ductware and
fittings to installers for residential and commercial purposes. All Air
has two branches and operates only in Southeast Queensland.

Complete Air Supply and All Air (together, the Parties) both supply of
HVAC ductware and fittings products in the South-East Queensland
region. HVAC ductware and fittings include flexible ducting, sheet
metal fittings, cushion boxes, grilles, diffusers, copper, zoning and
accessories used by installers.
All Air supplies the same types of HVAC ductware and fittings
products as those supplied by the Complete Air Supply but does not
supply HVAC units.
The Parties both operate from branches on the Sunshine Coast in
Queensland, with Complete Air Supply located in Bells Creek and All
Air located in Warana.
In addition to the Parties’ branches on the Sunshine Coast, Complete
Air Supply operates branches located in Burleigh on the Gold Coast
and Rockhampton in Queensland, and Tweed Heads South in New
South Wales. All Air also operates a branch in Geebung, in the
Greater Brisbane area.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The market share aggregation resulting from the Acquisition is
estimated to be low in the relevant markets.
• Post-Acquisition, the merged entity would continue to face
competition from multiple alternative suppliers of HVAC
ductware and fittings across south-east Queensland.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
